limited_overlap.description: applicants with prior_earnings between 45,100 and 1,062,290: 89% of the 2401 training applicants there have an enrolment propensity outside the overlap bounds, so the effect for them rests on the outcome model rather than on comparable enrolled and non-enrolled applicants.

applicants with months_unemployed equal to 0: 53% of the 1340 training applicants there have an enrolment propensity outside the overlap bounds, so the effect for them rests on the outcome model rather than on comparable enrolled and non-enrolled applicants.
applicants whose follow-up earnings are not recorded: their effect is identified only if non-response is unrelated to earnings given the adjustment set and enrolment (1881 training applicants).

warnings: Enrolled and non-enrolled applicants differ in pre-enrolment columns: mean prior earnings 17,847 against 37,489; the estimates adjust for the columns listed under roles.
experience is an exact linear combination of the other pre-enrolment columns; it is not put in the adjustment set, and its information is carried by the columns it is built from.
Candidates ['ethnicity'] passed the joint-test rule, but the R-learner smooth on them does not beat a constant effect by more than one SE (gain -11,495, SE 75,003); none is claimed.

No covariate passed the claim rule (joint p below 0.05 in the primary fit, at the median of four nuisance fits, with one sign). Candidates by median joint p: ethnicity p=0.0409 (+2538, +1194, +2647, +3340 dollars per SD); prior_earnings p=0.102 (+4736, +5659, +1713, +1321 dollars per SD); region p=0.294 (-1946, +822, -1736, -2085 dollars per SD); age p=0.576 (-499, -1566, -206, -117 dollars per SD). The joint p-value of each covariate moved across fold splits (the single-split fit gave p near 0.004 for age and 0.03 for prior earnings), so no covariate is claimed as an effect modifier.
20.5% of training rows have a cross-fitted propensity outside the overlap bounds; the all-rows ATE depends on the outcome model in those rows, and the overlap-bounded estimate is 4,110 dollars.
Instrument check (distance_km, responders only): complier effect 3,087 dollars with 90% interval [-4,573, 10,748], against the ATE 6,026. The complier effect and the ATE are different quantities.
Certificate and hours worked are measured during or after the program and are mediators; they are not adjusted for, so the estimates are total effects that include the paths through them.

Test applicants differ from training applicants in means: prior_earnings 31,449.2 (train) against 25,778.7 (test); months_unemployed 2.8 (train) against 3.2 (test). Per-applicant effects for test applicants outside the training range are extrapolated.

Test applicants outside the propensity overlap bounds: 5.3%. 211 of the 800 applicants at the top of the cate order are among them; their effects come from the outcome model, not from comparable enrolled and non-enrolled applicants. Restricting the top group to the overlap region gives 800 applicants with mean cate 6,299 dollars.
Test applicants outside the training range of an effect-model term: 2.5%.

No covariate passed the modifier rule, so no effect modifier is claimed. The per-applicant effects and the ranking come from a model on the lead covariates ['ethnicity', 'prior_earnings', 'region'], whose evidence is weak; the ranking carries less information than the interval widths suggest.
